info.description:
> **Tip**: This documentation is designed for humans. To integrate with AI agents, provide them with the OpenAPI schema at https://api.explee.com/public/api/openapi.json instead.

 

Search millions of companies worldwide using natural language queries and structured filters!

**Rate limit**: 10000 requests per hour, 150 concurrent requests per organization. Timeout: 90s.

post.description:
Search for companies using structured definitions.

## How It Works

Provide a structured definition of your target companies in the `definition` field — our AI will find matching companies.
All other filters are optional.
See the request schema below for the full list of available filters.

**Definition examples:**
- `"YouTube video summarization tool"`
- `"electronic signature platform"`
- `"AI B2B SaaS"`
- `"real estate company"`


## AI Enrichment

Use the `criteria` parameter to score companies against custom criteria.
Each company will be evaluated and scored (0-5) with reasoning for each criterion.

## Pricing

- **First 10 results are free** (including AI enrichment)
- A **positive credit balance is required for every request**, free results included (an organization at 0 credits gets a 402)
- Entirely-free requests are limited per organization by plan: **free 50/day + 10/min · starter 200/day + 15/min · growth 500/day + 20/min · pro 750/day + 25/min · agency 1500/day + 30/min · enterprise 3000/day + 30/min** (429 beyond); billable requests are not affected
- **0.5 credits** per company after the first 10
- **+0.1 credits** per company per criterion after the first 10

Example: 150 companies with 2 criteria = 50 billable × (0.5 + 0.1 × 2) = 35 credits (first 10 are free)

Empty results = 0 credits.

## Deduplication

Pass dedup list ids in `exclude_lists` to skip companies you already own — they are not returned
and not charged. Free results zone does not apply. See the Deduplication endpoints.

Search for people (employees) at companies matching your criteria.

## How It Works

Provide `job_titles` in `people_filters` to find people by their role.
Use `company_filters.definition` to narrow down which companies to search.
Use `company_linkedin_ids` to restrict results to a specific list of company LinkedIn IDs.

**Job title examples:**
- `["Head of Sales", "VP Sales"]`
- `["CTO", "VP Engineering"]`
- `["Founder", "CEO"]`

## AI Enrichment

Use the `criteria` parameter in `people_filters` to score people against custom criteria.
Each person will be evaluated and scored (0-5) with reasoning for each criterion.

## Pricing

- **First 10 results are free** (including AI enrichment)
- A **positive credit balance is required for every request**, free results included (an organization at 0 credits gets a 402)
- Entirely-free requests are limited per organization by plan: **free 50/day + 10/min · starter 200/day + 15/min · growth 500/day + 20/min · pro 750/day + 25/min · agency 1500/day + 30/min · enterprise 3000/day + 30/min** (429 beyond); billable requests are not affected
- **1.0 credit** per person after the first 10
- **+0.1 credits** per person per criterion after the first 10

Example: 150 people with 2 criteria = 50 billable × (1.0 + 0.1 × 2) = 60 credits (first 10 are free)

Empty results = 0 credits.

## Deduplication

Pass dedup list ids in `exclude_lists` to skip people you already own — they are not returned
and not charged. A companies list excludes everyone at its domains. Free results zone does not apply.

get.description:
Check status and retrieve results for a batch request.

**Statuses (in meta.status):**
- `pending` — processing in progress, poll again in a few seconds
- `completed` — results ready, `contacts` array contains enriched data
- `failed` — error occurred, see `meta.error` for details

**Response structure:**
- `contacts` — null while pending, array when completed
- `meta.status` — current processing status
- `meta.error` — error description (null if no error)
- `meta.credits_charged` — credits used (only charged for found emails)

**Typical workflow:**
1. POST to submit batch, get `task_id`
2. GET with `task_id`, check `meta.status`
3. If `pending`, wait 2-5 seconds and poll again
4. When `completed`, read `contacts` array

post.description:
Create a campaign that Explee finds the leads for — the app's **New campaign**
button.

Only `project_id` and `name` are required. Explee drafts every targeting field
you leave out (offer, customer problem, criteria, example clients) from the name
and your project; a field you send replaces the draft (`[]` means "none").
Search `keywords` are always drafted from the name. Geography and company size
default to the project's.

Not idempotent: each call creates a new campaign. If a call times out, list the
project's campaigns before retrying.

**Lifecycle after this call** (`status` in `GET /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns`):
1. `discovery` — created, nothing runs yet. Review or edit it with
   `GET` / `PATCH /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/{campaign_id}`.
2. `POST …/campaigns/{campaign_id}/start` — Explee searches for leads. Works
   with Auto-manage campaigns on or off.
3. `review` — the lead list is ready. Approve it with
   `POST …/campaigns/{campaign_id}/approve`. With Auto-manage campaigns ON it
   is also approved automatically at the end of the project's review window
   (12 hours by default); with it OFF only `approve` sends it.
4. `outreach` — sending, within the campaign and project budgets.

`POST …/stop` at any point parks the campaign (`listening`); a later `start`
resumes it — from a stopped review that means sending without a further
approve.

Creation is free. Returns the campaign's full definition.

get.description:
Read everything that decides who a campaign contacts and what it says — the
app's **Campaign** tab in one call.

**Who it targets:** `offer`, `customer_problem`, `target_role`,
`target_geography`, `target_company_size`, `positive_criteria`,
`negative_criteria`, `example_clients`, and the derived `keywords`.

**What it says:** `instructions` (first email), `followup_instructions` (shared
by every follow-up), `language`, and the project-level `reply_instructions`.

**When it says it:** `schedule` (the send days) and `followups` (how many
emails the sequence has and how far apart — a project-level setting, the
same for every campaign of the project).

`targeting_editable` is `false` for a campaign built from your own imported
lead list — its audience is that list, so the targeting fields are locked.

Free, and the natural first call when auditing an account: one request per
campaign tells you whether it is aimed at the right people, before a single
email goes out.

patch.description:
Correct a campaign's definition — send only the fields you are changing.

An omitted field keeps its value; an empty string, empty list or `null` clears
it — except `name`, which a campaign always has, so clearing it is a `422`.
An unknown field name is rejected with `422` rather than silently ignored, so
a typo can never look like a successful write. Returns the full definition as
it now stands.

**Re-aiming costs leads.** Every field Explee searches with re-aims the
campaign, exactly as in the app: `name`, `offer`, `customer_problem`,
`target_role`, `target_geography`, `target_company_size`, `positive_criteria`,
`negative_criteria` and `example_clients`. A real change to any of them drops
the leads this campaign has not contacted yet and makes Explee search again.
Sending the value a field already has is not a change. Only `language` and
`schedule` change nothing about who is contacted. Emails already sent are never
affected, and contacts already in a sequence keep it.

**The new search is not instant.** On a running campaign it starts about 5
minutes after your *last* targeting change, so a series of edits costs one
search, not one per edit. Each further targeting change restarts that wait:
send all your changes, then leave the campaign alone. Until the search starts,
the campaign keeps its current `status` and lead pool; when it starts, `status`
turns `searching`. On a stopped campaign the new targeting applies when you
start it again; on a campaign not launched yet, at launch.

**A running campaign pauses for review.** When the new search finishes, a
campaign that was sending moves to `review` (`status_reason`
`re_search_from_outreach`) and sends nothing until its new lead list is
approved: `POST /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/{campaign_id}/approve`. With
Auto-manage campaigns ON it is also approved automatically at the end of the
project's review window (12 hours by default); with it OFF only `approve`
resumes sending.

The rule for this endpoint: **anything a person can edit on the campaign in the
app, you can edit here** — with the exceptions below, each of which exists
because the app validates it in a second step this endpoint cannot reproduce.

Read-only here: `instructions` and `followup_instructions` (the copy briefs —
the app moderates them right after saving and shows you the verdict; this
endpoint has no preview to show, and an unmoderated brief only fails later, at
send time), `target_url` and `reply_instructions` (their own two-step save),
`keywords` (Explee derives it; read-only in the app too) and `followups` (a
project-level setting shared by every campaign of the project: sending the
current values back is accepted, different ones are a `422`). Budget has
`PATCH /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/{campaign_id}/budget`, status has
`start` / `stop`. You can still SET the briefs when you create a campaign —
`POST /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/import` takes `instructions`,
`followup_instructions` and `language`.

post.description:
Create a new campaign from your own lead list (async).

Each call creates a **new** campaign in the given project — the campaign is
built for your leads only (no agent lead discovery) and starts sending
automatically once live, within your project budget.

**How it works:**
1. Submit `project_id`, a campaign `name`, and up to 30,000 `leads`
2. Receive a `task_id` immediately
3. Poll `GET /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/import/{task_id}` until `completed`
4. `result.campaign_id` is your new campaign — it appears in the campaigns list

in the app shows, so a list pushed from your CRM sits next to the CSVs your

already taken gets a `(2)` suffix rather than merging, and lists are
independent — the same person on two lists is suppressed until both are gone.
Delete a list you no longer want.

Each person needs at least one identifier: an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a full
name; a row left without a usable one (including a malformed address) comes back
in `skipped` instead of failing the whole batch. **Outreach stops on the email** — the name and LinkedIn fields are stored
but not actively used today; they are kept because a suppressed person is more
than their email address, and the day outreach runs somewhere other than email
(LinkedIn and the like) those are the fields that will match. To suppress
everyone at a company use the companies endpoint.

post.description:
Add a webhook: we POST each new event of the project to `url`, signed with the
webhook's own secret (returned here). A project can have up to
20 webhooks; they also appear in the app under
**Settings → Integrations**. Zapier REST hooks: subscribe with this call,
unsubscribe with `DELETE /autogtm/webhooks/{id}`.


**Events.** `hot_lead.received` — a lead replied and the reply is Hot. The
body is the lead exactly as `GET /autogtm/hot-leads` returns it, in an envelope:

```json
{"event": "hot_lead.received", "delivery_id": "…", "created_at": "…",
 "project_id": 12, "test": false, "lead": {…}}
```

Only leads that turn hot after the webhook was added are sent, each once per
webhook; earlier ones are in the hot-leads feed. A delivery that fails on our
side or gets a 5xx / 408 / 429 is retried for at least 6 hours; any other 3xx
or 4xx is your endpoint's answer and is not retried (`last_error` says why).


Webhooks need a plan with CRM push (Standard and up): otherwise `403`.

SuppressPersonItem.description:
One person on the suppress list — the same fields the CSV upload accepts.

``email`` is a plain string, not a validated address, on purpose: a single
malformed cell in a 10 000-row CRM sync must not 422 the whole ledger and
leave NOBODY suppressed. An unusable address is dropped and counted in
``skipped``, exactly as the CSV upload treats a bad cell.

not actively used today; they are there because the identity of a suppressed
person is not only their email — the moment outreach runs somewhere other
